summary_en: This note studies the asymptotic error of the left-endpoint Riemann sum for a \(C^2([0,1])\) function and computes \(\lim_{n\to\infty} nR_n\). It also discusses sharper asymptotic expansions using piecewise Taylor expansion and the Euler-Maclaurin summation formula.

problems.statement_en:
Let \(f\in C^2([0,1])\), and define
\[
R_n:=\int_0^1 f(t)\,\mathrm{d}t-\frac1n\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(k/n).
\]
Find
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty} nR_n.
\]
prerequisites: continuity and differentiability on closed intervals

key_techniques_discussed: Piecewise estimation of the Riemann-sum error
Asymptotic expansion of left-endpoint Riemann sums
